0.0.n: This country name combines with の to describe Neymar as Brazil’s treasure.

0.1.n: Links Brazil to 至宝, showing whose treasure Neymar is.

0.2.n: Used figuratively to praise Neymar as someone exceptionally valuable to Brazil.

0.4.n: The name of a Brazilian football player, identified here as Brazil’s treasure.

0.5.n: Marks Neymar as the person the club has in its ranks; English naturally uses with here.

0.6.n: This formal verb describes the club as having a distinguished player and directly modifies its name.

0.7.n: The first part of the French football club’s name, パリ・サンジェルマン.

0.9.n: The second part of the French football club’s name, not a separate team.

0.10.n: Identifies Paris Saint-Germain as the team making the visit to Japan.

0.11.n: A noun used as a sentence ending in news style; 来日した would explicitly say arrived in Japan.

1.0.n: Points back to Neymar, who was just introduced.

1.1.n: The same Brazilian player’s name is repeated to introduce his opponent.

1.2.n: Marks the opponent when used with 対戦する.

1.3.n: 対戦 plus する makes a verb meaning to compete against someone.

1.4.n: Turns the preceding verb phrase into a noun-like expression referring to the person facing Neymar.

1.5.n: Marks the one facing Neymar as the subject; the next line reveals his identity.

2.0.n: Combines with 最優秀選手 to set the worldwide scope of the praise.

2.1.n: Describes 選手; 最 adds the sense of most to 優秀, excellent.

2.2.n: Refers to a sports competitor, specifically a footballer here.

2.4.n: The name of a prestigious football award, written in katakana.

2.5.n: Marks the Ballon d’Or as the award received.

2.6.n: 度 counts occurrences here, not temperature or angles.

2.7.n: 受賞する becomes 受賞している, expressing an established record of winning rather than an action happening now.

2.8.n: The football player’s name completes the identification begun in the previous line.

0.lit: Brazil’s greatest treasure, Neymar, having in its ranks, Paris Saint-Germain arrives in Japan.
0.tip: The phrase ending in 擁する comes before the club’s name and describes which team is arriving.

1.lit: The one who faces that Neymar is…
1.tip: Verb + のが introduces someone by what they do, with their identity revealed next.

2.lit: World’s best player, Ballon d’Or five times having won, Cristiano Ronaldo.
2.tip: 受賞している describes Ronaldo’s accumulated achievement, not an award ceremony currently taking place.
